pull.title: wallet, rpc, gui: Allow users to manually rebroadcast a wallet transaction
pull.body: From the discussion in #36403, it is clear that there needs to be a way for users to rebroadcast a transaction. Currently, the way to do so requires getting the raw transaction, getting the hex, and using `sendrawtransaction`. This PR adds `rebroadcastwallettx` RPC that takes a txid to attempt to rebroadcast that single transaction. An action is also added to the GUI menu for each transaction to do the same.

Concept ACK

Whatever the solution of the existing issues with rebroadcast will be, giving the users the option to rebroadcast transactions manually is useful in all of these scenarios.

Concept ACK

One issue should be fixed before merge: `rebroadcastwallettx` fails with code -1 and an empty message when the transaction is out of the mempool and its feerate is above the wallet's `-maxfeerate`.

I ran the RPC on regtest at 648450039a. Other mempool rejections keep their reason, such as "bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent" for a child whose parent expired. The empty message shows up when a user lowers `-maxfeerate` to 20 sat/vB and restarts without mempool.dat. Our own 50 sat/vB child of an incoming payment then stays out of the mempool, and the RPC returns `{"code": -1, "message": ""}`. For the same transaction, `sendrawtransaction` with `maxfeerate=0.0002` returns -25 "Fee rate exceeds maximum configured by user (maxfeerate)".

The cause is that `Chain::broadcastTransaction` returns only a bool, and `BroadcastTransaction` sets no error string for `MAX_FEE_EXCEEDED` or `MAX_FEE_RATE_EXCEEDED`. `sendrawtransaction` falls back to `TransactionErrorString` in that case. The wallet's other callers only log the string or drop it, so this RPC is the first to show it to a user. The same fallback inside the `Chain::broadcastTransaction` wrapper would fix it, and the GUI action will need that message once it shows the result. I can share the probe script.
